title: GO AT ONCE AND TAKE A LAMB

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and said to them, 'Go at once and
select the animals for your families and slaughter the Passover lamb. Take a
bunch of hyssop, dip it into the blood in the basin and put some of the blood on
the top and on both sides of the doorframe. None of you shall go out of the door
of your house until morning.'" - Ex 12:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses passes on the instruction, and two details stand out.

First, the hyssop. It was a common, humble plant, nothing impressive, used for
sprinkling. God did not require a golden instrument. He used what was already
growing by the wall. Later, David would pray, "Cleanse me with hyssop, and I
will be clean" (Ps 51:7). And at the cross, when Jesus said He was thirsty, they
lifted a sponge to His lips on a stalk of hyssop (John 19:29). The humble plant
appears at both ends of the story.

Second: "None of you shall go out of the door of your house until morning." The
blood was on the door, and they had to stay under it. There was safety, but only
inside. A man who decided to step out that night to see what was happening would
have been outside the covering.

This is not a threat so much as a picture. Our security is in Christ, and it is
found by remaining in Him. Jesus said, "Remain in me, as I also remain in you"
(John 15:4). Faith is not a single decision at the door followed by wandering
off. It is staying where the blood has placed us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you living inside the shelter God has given, or wandering out of it?
2. What humble means has God used to bless you that you overlooked?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, thank You for the shelter of Your blood. Help me to remain in You
and not wander from the safety You have given. Amen.
